summary: DeFi is an instruction-only, advisory skill that analyzes DeFi protocol risk, decomposes headline APY into real net yield, screens for rug-risk patterns and categorizes tax events from transaction logs the user pastes in. It declares and needs no environment variables, API keys, wallets, binaries or network hosts, and the files contain no scripts, downloads, encoded payloads or outbound calls. Its only links are a GitHub homepage in skill.json and a ClawHub publisher URL in skill-card.md, and it repeatedly disclaims any wallet, seed-phrase or private-key handling.

findings.message: The skill states it never asks for a seed phrase, private key or wallet secret and has no signing or broadcasting logic, so no wallet credential handling is requested; users are told to sign locally with their own tooling.

The skill card lists the risk that users may paste wallet secrets while asking for help and tells them not to share seed phrases, private keys or signing material, which confirms the skill itself does not need them.
skill.json names the author as "qclawbot" and points the homepage at github.com/qclawbot/defi-skill, while the registry owner shown elsewhere is @agisearch, so publisher identity is inconsistent.

The skill says any chain or protocol context supplied by the host platform should be treated as read-only analysis context, but it declares no tool, host or key for this and the data source is left undefined.
The tax feature processes CSV, export or text transaction logs that the user supplies, which can contain wallet addresses and financial history, but it does no chain indexing or outbound transfer.
